sources.authorityAssessment: Society resource guide, not a formal systematic guideline. Targeted nodal-status recommendation and discussion of ASTRO guidance: node-positive invasive cancer is outside the routine partial-breast-only recommendation. No copied selection table, exact dose or fractionation rule.

claims.statement: A breast-cancer axillary nodal deposit larger than 0.2 mm and no larger than 2 mm is micrometastatic; a deposit larger than 2 mm exceeds that category.
claims.limitation: Single government source for this exact size definition; size category is not itself a universal ALND rule. Constructed measurements are not new clinical thresholds.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: For pure DCIS treated with breast conservation and whole-breast radiation, a negative margin of at least 2 mm is adequate without routine widening.
claims.limitation: Do not extend this to omission of radiation or an automatic operation for every narrower negative margin.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Tumor at a final radial inked boundary after lumpectomy generally warrants further excision when residual breast tissue remains.
claims.limitation: A true anterior/posterior anatomic boundary without remaining breast tissue and individualized competing risks require separate assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: An oriented additional cavity specimen can establish a new final external boundary; the original specimen distance must be reconciled with that boundary.
claims.limitation: Single adequate source; the exact constructed orientation is explicit. A loosely labelled fragment cannot silently replace a final margin.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: In US breast-conserving treatment of invasive carcinoma with an associated DCIS component, absence of tumor on ink generally satisfies the margin standard.
claims.limitation: Not the pure-DCIS or DCIS-microinvasion rule; residual suspicious imaging and extensive close disease still need clinical assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Conventional DCIS management usually omits sentinel surgery for uncomplicated lumpectomy and includes it with mastectomy because subsequent mapping may fail.
claims.limitation: Single current source; planned delayed SPIO mapping and specific invasion/mapping concerns are exceptions, not universal rules.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: After upfront breast conservation, selected clinically node-negative invasive cancers with one or two positive sentinel nodes and planned whole-breast radiation can avoid completion dissection.
claims.limitation: The case supplies small primary, no gross extranodal disease and systemic treatment. This does not extend Z0011 to post-NST residual disease or heavier nodal burden.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: For selected upfront mastectomy patients with one or two positive sentinel nodes, regional nodal irradiation can support omission of completion dissection.
claims.limitation: Single adequate 2026 society source; radiation commitment and trial-population applicability matter. Omission is not an unconditional mastectomy rule.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: After NST in initially node-positive, now clinically node-negative noninflammatory cancer, targeted removal of the clipped node with optimized sentinel mapping improves staging reliability.
claims.limitation: Single current source. Dual mapping and retrieval of more than two sentinel nodes reduce false negatives; a negative ultrasound cannot establish ypN0.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Residual sentinel-node micro- or macrometastasis after NST remains an indication for completion axillary dissection in current ASBrS guidance.
claims.limitation: Single current source; not isolated tumor cells. Mature randomized replacement-by-radiation evidence was not established by the retrieved guide.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: A clinically node-negative axilla after NST still ordinarily undergoes sentinel staging, even with a radiographic breast response.
claims.limitation: Single current source; investigational omission populations are not automatically standard care.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Pretreatment clinically bulky or fixed biopsy-proven axillary disease and inflammatory disease do not acquire the usual cN1 de-escalation pathway solely through response.
claims.limitation: Single current society source; sparse cN2-3 sentinel data. Exact pretreatment examination must be retained.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: For a substantial HER2-positive, node-positive nonmetastatic primary, neoadjuvant chemotherapy with HER2-directed therapy is an established treatment approach.
claims.limitation: No universal regimen, dose, interval or complete medical eligibility rule is authored. This is not a recommendation for every small HER2-positive tumor.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Residual invasive HER2-positive cancer after taxane/trastuzumab-based neoadjuvant treatment supports adjuvant ado-trastuzumab emtansine consideration.
claims.limitation: Oncology referral/selection rather than automatic administration. Residual DCIS alone does not meet this indication; toxicity and eligibility review remain necessary.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Breast surgery after NST integrates original proven sites and current residual distribution; imaging response does not authorize omission of definitive local surgery.
claims.limitation: Single adequate current source; no modality is universally mandatory and imaging does not prove microscopic clearance.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Diffuse malignant calcifications can preclude breast conservation despite disappearance of a previously enhancing invasive mass.
claims.limitation: Single current source; extent and malignant tissue verification are supplied. Limited multifocal disease is not automatically a mastectomy indication.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: When an additional imaging focus would change the breast operation, representative tissue verification and imaging-pathology concordance should precede escalation based on that focus.
claims.limitation: Single adequate government assessment source; its screening setting is narrower than these surgical applications. No universal routine-MRI recommendation is made.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Localization and specimen imaging should confirm removal of the intended nonpalpable lesion; the marker identity must be reconciled with its documented relation to that lesion.
claims.limitation: Two guides from one society are not independent corroboration. Constructed positional data establish the target relation; marker presence or absence alone is insufficient.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Persistent unilateral nipple skin abnormalities require representative skin tissue evaluation; a parenchymal sample lacking epidermis does not resolve that surface target.
claims.limitation: The exact sample-content application is original reasoning from tissue provenance. No mandatory punch-versus-wedge superiority is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Confirmed Paget disease requires assessment for underlying breast carcinoma, including additional imaging when conventional studies do not establish its extent.
claims.limitation: MRI is an adjunct for this unresolved extent, not a universal first test or proof of absence of invasion.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Paget treatment must address the involved nipple skin and underlying carcinoma; selected localized disease can undergo an appropriately encompassing breast-conserving resection with radiation.
claims.limitation: No automatic nipple-sparing pathway. Exact central resection suitability and cosmetic consequences require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Rapid diffuse breast skin changes require tissue diagnosis and extent assessment; a nonrepresentative benign sample cannot settle a persistent suspicious parenchymal target.
claims.limitation: Do not use the skin findings alone as histologic proof. No formal proposed diagnostic score or mandatory symptom-duration cutoff is imported.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Nonmetastatic inflammatory breast cancer is ordinarily treated with systemic therapy before modified radical mastectomy and postoperative radiation.
claims.limitation: Reassuring response does not erase the original phenotype. No fixed reconstruction timeline is supported here.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: After primary breast cancer treatment, asymptomatic follow-up uses clinical assessment and appropriate breast mammography rather than routine systemic scans or tumor-marker screening.
claims.limitation: Single adequate government source in this ledger; new symptoms or abnormal examination require a separate diagnostic assessment. No exact first-postradiation interval is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Recurrent breast cancer may change receptor status, so current tumor tissue can require repeat biomarker assessment for treatment planning.
claims.limitation: Single adequate government source; no exact metastatic regimen is ranked. Germline blood testing does not establish the receptor phenotype of a recurrent tumor.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Hormone-receptor-negative breast cancer does not acquire an endocrine-treatment indication from an earlier receptor-positive specimen, and HER2 tumor testing informs HER2-directed treatment.
claims.limitation: Current adequate tumor evaluation governs planning; this does not compare evolving drug regimens or resolve low-expression assay categories.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Extended adjuvant neratinib after trastuzumab-based therapy is a different treatment phase from response-adapted T-DM1 consideration for residual invasive disease immediately after NST.
claims.limitation: Targeted phase distinction only; not a recommendation to give neratinib or a current head-to-head regimen ranking.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Current ASBrS guidance recognizes selected post-NST, clinically node-negative patients with initially proven nodal disease who can have acceptable sentinel staging with at least three negative sentinel nodes even when clipping or clipped-node retrieval was not performed.
claims.limitation: Single current society resource. This does not establish a universal missing-clip rescue operation or let a normal scan replace pathology; the exact technical situation still needs clinical assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Selected initially node-positive patients after NST, distinct from inflammatory or initial bulky/fixed disease.

claims.statement: A negative receptor result from decalcified breast-cancer bone tissue needs preanalytic scrutiny; an available nondecalcified metastatic tumor sample can provide more suitable material for repeat predictive assays.
claims.limitation: Decalcification does not invalidate every result. Assay validation and the actual process matter; no exact minimum tumor-cell count or processing-time threshold is invented.
claims.applicablePopulation: Recurrent breast cancer with discordant receptor studies and available metastatic tissue.

claims.statement: Routine partial-breast-only irradiation is not the recommended substitute for whole-breast treatment in an invasive breast cancer with pathologically positive nodes.
claims.limitation: Single directly verified current society source. No claim that every positive node requires ALND or regional nodal irradiation; the whole clinical population still matters.
claims.applicablePopulation: Invasive cancer after lumpectomy with a positive sentinel node, outside a study protocol.

claims.statement: For substantial node-positive HER2-positive cancer selected for neoadjuvant treatment, chemotherapy is combined with HER2-directed therapy; ideally the systemic regimen is completed before surgery.
claims.limitation: The NCI overview includes chemotherapy-free dual-blockade trial arms; their existence does not establish that splitting chemotherapy until after surgery is the preferred routine sequence. No dose or cycle count is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Medically eligible nonmetastatic HER2-positive node-positive cancer before treatment.

claims.statement: In selected upfront-surgery patients with limited positive sentinel nodes, a radiation-supported omission strategy avoids adding the morbidity of completion dissection to an applicable radiation plan.
claims.limitation: Patient goals and exact radiation field matter; this is not a universal radiation-versus-surgery ranking or a post-NST residual-disease omission rule.
claims.applicablePopulation: Eligible upfront breast conservation or selected mastectomy with limited sentinel involvement.

claims.statement: A breast-cancer axillary nodal deposit larger than 0.2 mm and no larger than 2 mm is micrometastatic; a deposit larger than 2 mm exceeds that category.
claims.limitation: Single government source for this exact size definition; size category is not itself a universal ALND rule. Constructed measurements are not new clinical thresholds.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: For pure DCIS treated with breast conservation and whole-breast radiation, a negative margin of at least 2 mm is adequate without routine widening.
claims.limitation: Do not extend this to omission of radiation or an automatic operation for every narrower negative margin.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Tumor at a final radial inked boundary after lumpectomy generally warrants further excision when residual breast tissue remains.
claims.limitation: A true anterior/posterior anatomic boundary without remaining breast tissue and individualized competing risks require separate assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: An oriented additional cavity specimen can establish a new final external boundary; the original specimen distance must be reconciled with that boundary.
claims.limitation: Single adequate source; the exact constructed orientation is explicit. A loosely labelled fragment cannot silently replace a final margin.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: In US breast-conserving treatment of invasive carcinoma with an associated DCIS component, absence of tumor on ink generally satisfies the margin standard.
claims.limitation: Not the pure-DCIS or DCIS-microinvasion rule; residual suspicious imaging and extensive close disease still need clinical assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Conventional DCIS management usually omits sentinel surgery for uncomplicated lumpectomy and includes it with mastectomy because subsequent mapping may fail.
claims.limitation: Single current source; planned delayed SPIO mapping and specific invasion/mapping concerns are exceptions, not universal rules.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: After upfront breast conservation, selected clinically node-negative invasive cancers with one or two positive sentinel nodes and planned whole-breast radiation can avoid completion dissection.
claims.limitation: The case supplies small primary, no gross extranodal disease and systemic treatment. This does not extend Z0011 to post-NST residual disease or heavier nodal burden.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: For selected upfront mastectomy patients with one or two positive sentinel nodes, regional nodal irradiation can support omission of completion dissection.
claims.limitation: Single adequate 2026 society source; radiation commitment and trial-population applicability matter. Omission is not an unconditional mastectomy rule.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: After NST in initially node-positive, now clinically node-negative noninflammatory cancer, targeted removal of the clipped node with optimized sentinel mapping improves staging reliability.
claims.limitation: Single current source. Dual mapping and retrieval of more than two sentinel nodes reduce false negatives; a negative ultrasound cannot establish ypN0.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Residual sentinel-node micro- or macrometastasis after NST remains an indication for completion axillary dissection in current ASBrS guidance.
claims.limitation: Single current source; not isolated tumor cells. Mature randomized replacement-by-radiation evidence was not established by the retrieved guide.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: A clinically node-negative axilla after NST still ordinarily undergoes sentinel staging, even with a radiographic breast response.
claims.limitation: Single current source; investigational omission populations are not automatically standard care.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Pretreatment clinically bulky or fixed biopsy-proven axillary disease and inflammatory disease do not acquire the usual cN1 de-escalation pathway solely through response.
claims.limitation: Single current society source; sparse cN2-3 sentinel data. Exact pretreatment examination must be retained.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: For a substantial HER2-positive, node-positive nonmetastatic primary, neoadjuvant chemotherapy with HER2-directed therapy is an established treatment approach.
claims.limitation: No universal regimen, dose, interval or complete medical eligibility rule is authored. This is not a recommendation for every small HER2-positive tumor.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Residual invasive HER2-positive cancer after taxane/trastuzumab-based neoadjuvant treatment supports adjuvant ado-trastuzumab emtansine consideration.
claims.limitation: Oncology referral/selection rather than automatic administration. Residual DCIS alone does not meet this indication; toxicity and eligibility review remain necessary.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Breast surgery after NST integrates original proven sites and current residual distribution; imaging response does not authorize omission of definitive local surgery.
claims.limitation: Single adequate current source; no modality is universally mandatory and imaging does not prove microscopic clearance.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Diffuse malignant calcifications can preclude breast conservation despite disappearance of a previously enhancing invasive mass.
claims.limitation: Single current source; extent and malignant tissue verification are supplied. Limited multifocal disease is not automatically a mastectomy indication.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: When an additional imaging focus would change the breast operation, representative tissue verification and imaging-pathology concordance should precede escalation based on that focus.
claims.limitation: Single adequate government assessment source; its screening setting is narrower than these surgical applications. No universal routine-MRI recommendation is made.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Localization and specimen imaging should confirm removal of the intended nonpalpable lesion; the marker identity must be reconciled with its documented relation to that lesion.
claims.limitation: Two guides from one society are not independent corroboration. Constructed positional data establish the target relation; marker presence or absence alone is insufficient.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Persistent unilateral nipple skin abnormalities require representative skin tissue evaluation; a parenchymal sample lacking epidermis does not resolve that surface target.
claims.limitation: The exact sample-content application is original reasoning from tissue provenance. No mandatory punch-versus-wedge superiority is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Confirmed Paget disease requires assessment for underlying breast carcinoma, including additional imaging when conventional studies do not establish its extent.
claims.limitation: MRI is an adjunct for this unresolved extent, not a universal first test or proof of absence of invasion.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Paget treatment must address the involved nipple skin and underlying carcinoma; selected localized disease can undergo an appropriately encompassing breast-conserving resection with radiation.
claims.limitation: No automatic nipple-sparing pathway. Exact central resection suitability and cosmetic consequences require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Rapid diffuse breast skin changes require tissue diagnosis and extent assessment; a nonrepresentative benign sample cannot settle a persistent suspicious parenchymal target.
claims.limitation: Do not use the skin findings alone as histologic proof. No formal proposed diagnostic score or mandatory symptom-duration cutoff is imported.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Nonmetastatic inflammatory breast cancer is ordinarily treated with systemic therapy before modified radical mastectomy and postoperative radiation.
claims.limitation: Reassuring response does not erase the original phenotype. No fixed reconstruction timeline is supported here.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: After primary breast cancer treatment, asymptomatic follow-up uses clinical assessment and appropriate breast mammography rather than routine systemic scans or tumor-marker screening.
claims.limitation: Single adequate government source in this ledger; new symptoms or abnormal examination require a separate diagnostic assessment. No exact first-postradiation interval is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Recurrent breast cancer may change receptor status, so current tumor tissue can require repeat biomarker assessment for treatment planning.
claims.limitation: Single adequate government source; no exact metastatic regimen is ranked. Germline blood testing does not establish the receptor phenotype of a recurrent tumor.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Hormone-receptor-negative breast cancer does not acquire an endocrine-treatment indication from an earlier receptor-positive specimen, and HER2 tumor testing informs HER2-directed treatment.
claims.limitation: Current adequate tumor evaluation governs planning; this does not compare evolving drug regimens or resolve low-expression assay categories.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

claims.statement: Extended adjuvant neratinib after trastuzumab-based therapy is a different treatment phase from response-adapted T-DM1 consideration for residual invasive disease immediately after NST.
claims.limitation: Targeted phase distinction only; not a recommendation to give neratinib or a current head-to-head regimen ranking.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly stated breast-cancer care phase; fixed synthetic clinic chart-review profiles.

sourceRechecks.scope: Limited positive-node mastectomy with RNI; upfront BCS/WBRT omission; residual post-NST micrometastasis positive ALND indication; clip retrieval not universal if three or more negative sentinel nodes.
Combined neoadjuvant chemotherapy/HER2 therapy before surgery, trial dual-blockade arms and axillary morbidity.
Diffuse malignant calcifications versus selected multifocal conservation.

reviewResponse.publicationCounting: ASCO 2015 guideline is one older formal publication used only for the specific processing principle. Multiple ASBrS documents remain one authority; no alias is independent corroboration.

parks.attempt: Removed the redundant no-NST sentence and tried a regional-plan set: completion ALND, regional reirradiation, or no further regional treatment.
parks.reason: The specialist's actual reirradiation exclusion makes that third plan inapplicable; repeating mapping or limited arbitrary sampling remains filler. A fair difficult three-choice comparison was not established without changing the clinical premise or inventing another acceptable procedure.
parks.nextAction: Retain the legitimate binary teaching boundary as an unkeyed authoring gap; obtain a source-supported third policy or a specifically accepted foundational format before authoring again.

parks.attempt: Removed the unused breast marker and tried a failed-mapping/result-adequacy follow-up instead of the simple normal-examination staging choice.
parks.reason: The supplied facts still do not establish a concrete acquisition failure. Adding one would require a verified next-action criterion distinguishing remapping, completion dissection and acceptance; the current source supports optimized technique but not the invented failure workflow. The original remains easy recall without an accepted basic exception.
parks.nextAction: Keep the cN0 staging gap visible; do not emit a keyed invented failure-management item.

parks.attempt: Replaced the named unsampled target with a proposed needle-path/specimen record and replaced aspiration with repeat core, open incisional sampling and additional skin punches.
parks.reason: That attempt duplicates the already preserved breast-core-discordance objective, while the supplied evidence does not establish a uniquely ranked repeat-core versus incisional plan in a genuinely difficult new case. Simply hiding the compartment or removing the fluid negative would reduce fairness rather than add inference.
parks.nextAction: Preserve the exact inflammatory treatment-sequence PASS separately. Revisit diagnostic expansion only with supported acquisition data and three credible tissue plans.

parks.attempt: Tried comparing superficial, punch and wedge specimens with different represented tissues instead of announcing missing epidermis.
parks.reason: No supported observation fairly ranks adequate punch against wedge, and an obviously epidermis-free sample recreates the same one-step compartment match. A harder adequate-sample/extent decision was not established without new clinical criteria.
parks.nextAction: Keep the Paget biopsy gap unkeyed rather than claim a new basic acceptance or fabricate a preferred biopsy technique.

parks.attempt: Replaced the feasibility/missing-biopsy sentences with the proposed resection geometry and tried same-stage second-look imaging, additional-target biopsy and primary-target reassessment.
parks.reason: The primary has no actual adequacy problem; repeating it is still filler. Distinguishing second-look imaging from image-guided biopsy needs an actual supported acquisition/visibility record. The attempted rewrite did not establish that prerequisite fairly.
parks.nextAction: Split the exact benign-sample-discordance PASS into a self-contained case. Commission a distinct supported imaging-acquisition dilemma rather than reuse its target-provenance answer.

parks.attempt: Added a proposed pretreatment calcification map and compared residual-field sampling, current-enhancement sampling and direct image-localized excision.
parks.reason: If the field was already known malignant, the added biopsy need is not established; if not characterized, the exact post-NST sampling-to-resection implication still requires clinician confirmation. Negative selected cores must not be invented as permission to leave a suspicious field.
parks.nextAction: Park this workflow. The separate revised operation case starts with already acquired mapped malignant tissue and does not imply an unverified diagnostic algorithm.

parks.attempt: Removed the critique-style without label and tried a mapping-adequacy version with negative sentinel specimens but an unretrieved original clip.
parks.reason: The current ASBrS guide allows adequate staging in selected patients with three or more negative sentinel nodes even without clip retrieval. A missing clip is therefore not a universal dissection/retrieval trigger. Changing the count or inventing an immediate rescue sequence would not establish a uniquely ranked action from the supplied facts.
parks.nextAction: Preserve the exact later residual-HER2 PASS independently. Ask for an explicitly supported technical retrieval/failure scenario before another keyed staging-adequacy draft.
